unit: Mg ha-1 (aboveground live tree biomass, FIADB DRYBIO_AG basis)
method: Generic aboveground live tree biomass yield curves fitted to FIA remeasurement intervals on single condition forested plots, by forest type group and USDA Forest Service ecological section, 0 to 250 yr. Curve: AGB(t) = min(cap, exp(mu_type + u_cell) x f(t)), where f is the chosen decline-capable form (CR, CRS, CRD or HG) under strategy S1 (remeasurement only, algebraic difference) or S2 (joint chronosequence plus repeated measures mixed model). Every curve is capped at the type's observed 99th percentile AGB; values beyond each cell's 99th percentile observed stand age are flagged as extrapolations. The 95% band is a plot cluster bootstrap confidence interval on the median curve (200 resamples, shape and level refit on each plot draw; draws failing the early rise screen are dropped). PI90 is a 90% prediction interval for a single plot. The median curve is the typical plot; the mean curve multiplies it by exp((s_plot^2 + s_res^2)/2) and is the right input for population totals. These are population curves: equivalence tests on annual net change fail the slope test for every candidate, so they do not predict plot level change.

notes: ME: curves from the Maine workbook Curves_5yr sheet (section ALL is the statewide curve). cap and age_q99 come from the Caps sheet, which gives them per type; age_q99 is carried on the ALL curve only and is null for section cells, whose extrapolation flags mark the cell's own 99th percentile age. dropped_early for ME is 200 minus the surviving bootstrap draws.

MI, WI, MN: curves from final_curves_capped_lakes_DATA.csv (section ALL is the statewide curve). MN maple-beech-birch and oak rows in that file are the Lake States pooled fit (LSPOOL, S1 HG), limited to MN cells and re-capped at the MN 99th percentile AGB; the MN state fits for those two types failed the early rise screen and were rejected. Their picks carry pooled: 'LSPOOL'. The pooled bootstrap decline summary exists for MBB only (119 of 200 draws); none is carried for MN oak. Lake States label type group 100 white-red-jack pine (type_labels).

NH, VT: curves from final_curves_capped_NHVT_long_DATA.csv (section ALL is the state curve). Shapes were fitted on NH and VT pooled with a state level effect (NH about 5% above VT), so the pick and bootstrap decline tables are shared by both states (pooled: 'NHVT'). Elm-ash-cottonwood (16 pooled plots) was dropped under the 50 plot thin rule and has no NH or VT curve. Oak: every candidate failed the 99.9th percentile magnitude screen; the curve is held at the type cap.
